chunks: From him, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Yusuf ibn Aqil, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) ruled regarding a man and a woman whose house collapsed on them, causing both to die, and it was not known which of them died first. He said: 'Each of them inherits the other, as Allah has prescribed for their heirs.'
ai.seo_question: How is inheritance distributed when a husband and wife die simultaneously and the order of death is unknown?
ai.summary: This ruling from Imam Ali (AS) in *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the principle of *ta'arush* (mutual inheritance) for simultaneous death (*al-khala'*) where the order of death is indeterminate, ensuring both spouses inherit from each other before their respective families. This legal precedent highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on equitable distribution and the presumption of co-existence in the absence of definitive evidence, a concept foundational to Islamic inheritance jurisprudence.
